summary.text: Mike Simpson is the Republican U.S. Representative for Idaho's 2nd District, serving since 1999, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.

Born in Burley and raised in Blackfoot, he worked as a dentist, served on the Blackfoot City Council and in the Idaho Legislature, and was Speaker of the Idaho House before his election to Congress. He chairs the House Appropriations subcommittee on Interior and Environment.

paragraphs.text: Simpson was born in Burley, Idaho, and raised in Blackfoot, where his father was a dentist.

According to Wikipedia, he graduated from Blackfoot High School, Utah State University (1972), and the Washington University School of Dental Medicine in St. Louis (1977); his official biography confirms the university and dental degrees.
He practiced dentistry in Blackfoot, joining his father and uncle at the Simpson Family Dental Practice.

Simpson began his political career in 1980 with his election to the Blackfoot City Council, and he served in the Idaho Legislature from 1984 to 1998, including his last six years as Speaker of the Idaho House.
He was elected to the U.S. House in 1998 and took office in January 1999; his official biography says he is serving his fourteenth term.

He sits on the House Appropriations Committee, where he chairs the Interior and Environment Subcommittee and is a member of the Energy and Water Development and the Labor, Health and Human Services, Education subcommittees.
According to his official biography, Simpson has been married to his wife, Kathy, for more than 50 years, and the couple has lived in Idaho their whole lives.

He won re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election with 51.7% of the vote to Ellie Gilbreath's 40.3%, Tripp Hutchinson's 3.5%, Emre Houser's 2.4% and Will Johanson's 2.2%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
